focal_character.name: Wanjiku Mwangi
focal_character.occupation: Records Coordination Lead at a public hospital in Nairobi
focal_character.ordinary_life_state: In a Ministry budget review meeting, Wanjiku separates a fused three-signature motion into individual approval lines, crosses out all but one, and identifies the County Board signature as the binding one — the motion passes in six minutes.

problem_structure.unknown: Which of the three fused conditions — seal, stamp, or audit date — is the single binding clause
data: A metal panel with engraved text listing three requirements fused as one directive
Three walls of shelving stacked with brown document boxes grouped by department, year, and audit files
A filing card stack and the most recent audit date visible on the audit shelf box
An indicator light system that responds differently to each clause tested individually
problem_structure.condition: All three requirements are presented as a single fused directive; satisfying all three simultaneously stalls, but only one actually binds — the gate does not reveal which until each clause is isolated and tested alone

gate_details.correct_approach: Separate the fused condition into individual clauses by physically covering each one with a palm, ask whether the gate requires each clause alone, observe which clause triggers the gate's response — the audit date — and satisfy only that clause to close the gate.

new_texture: Ministry budget review meetings on Kenyatta Avenue are held in rooms with non-functional projectors where fused multi-signature motions routinely stall until someone separates the requirements into individual approval lines.
A Records Coordination Lead nameplate — black lettering on gold — marks the desk where memos now land first instead of the third-floor clerk stack, a visible step up in responsibility.
Inter-departmental budget negotiations stall when each representative waits for another to commit first; naming the single binding signature unblocks the entire group without explanation.
